title: Temporal alignment of gesture with discourse structure in naturalistic communication
titleZh: 自然交流中手势与话语结构的时间对齐
abstract: Abstract How discourse is reorganized in real time remains difficult to observe directly because discourse transitions are typically identified from linguistic content rather than continuous behavior. Although gesture is a fundamental component of human communication, it remains unclear whether the timing and intensity of hand movement systematically change around such transitions in naturalistic settings. We addressed this question by using automated pose estimation to extract continuous hand-movement signals from mathematics and literature classroom instruction and aligning them with independently annotated discourse boundaries. Brief bursts of unusually strong hand movement occurred more often near high-confidence discourse boundaries than during other analyzed portions of the lessons, showing that manual activity clustered around moments of discourse reorganization. This boundary-centered pattern was reproducible within individual teachers across multiple lessons, although its precise shape differed across teachers and was similar in mathematics and literature instruction despite differences in communicative content. Collectively, these findings suggest that the timing of hand movement may provide an observable behavioral correlate of discourse organization and show that automated continuous-movement analysis offers a scalable way to investigate how naturalistic communication unfolds over time. More broadly, the results are consistent with theoretical accounts that view human communication as multimodal, embodied, and dynamically coordinated.
summaryZh: 高置信度话语边界附近出现异常强手部运动短促爆发的频率高于课程其他分析片段，即手部活动聚集于话语重组时刻。 该以边界为中心的模式在个别教师的多节课内可重复，但具体形态因教师而异。 数学与文学讲授中该模式相似，尽管交流内容不同。 作者据此提出手部运动的时间可能提供话语组织的可观察行为相关物，并认为结果与多模态、具身、动态协调的交流理论相一致。
